chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his fathers (peace be upon them), who said:
The infant is inherited from and prayer is offered over him if he falls from his mother's womb and cries out; and if he does not cry out, he is not inherited from and prayer is not offered over him.

key_terms.فَاسْتَهَلَّ: And cried out / uttered a cry
key_terms.يُصَلَّى عَلَيْهِ: Prayer is offered over him (Funeral prayer)

ai.seo_question: What are the conditions for offering funeral prayer over a newborn infant in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic status of a fetus upon birth, establishing that audible crying (istihlal) serves as the definitive proof of life for inheritance and funeral prayer. In Shia fiqh, this criterion distinguishes between a stillborn and a live-born infant, ensuring the deceased is treated with the full rites of a Muslim. The ruling underscores the importance of physical signs of life in determining legal rights and obligations within the family structure.
